cues.text: This is Flask 3.1.3 in Visual Studio Code, with the *Moon panel* on the left.
First, *Stop*. I start an inline edit and press Stop while Moon is working.
Moon stops at once: *the file was not changed*.
git status is *clean*.
Task A. I select get_debug_flag, press Control I, and paste the instruction.
The diff is drawn *in the file*: green lines added, red lines removed, with *Accept and Reject on every hunk*.
I accept each hunk on its own. *Nothing is written* until I accept.
With FLASK_DEBUG set to off, get_debug_flag now returns *False*.
I restore the file. git status is clean again.
Task B, agent mode. The request *names no files*.
Before any model call, Moon packs a ranked *project map* into an eight thousand token budget.
A *scout subagent* searches and reads the code. Each tool call is one line in the live log.
The *context card* shows the files the scout chose, code, tests and docs, why each one, and the token budget.
The agent edited a *hidden copy* and ran pytest: verified. Apply changes opens the review: six hunks in *three files I never named*.
I press Apply. *Only the accepted hunks* reach my files.
Moon's summary says what changed, and what it did not check.
In the terminal, flask help lists the new *config* command, and flask config prints the configuration as JSON, with *secrets masked*.
This is the same run in *TrueForge's own UI*: the scout subagent, then every *MCP tool call*, from search to apply changes.
Back in the editor, *Undo this whole run* puts all three files back.
git status is *clean*.
Task C. This script gives the main Claude provider an *invalid key* in TrueForge.
I repeat Task A.
Claude fails, and Moon switches to *DeepSeek on Azure* by itself, on a new TrueForge session. *Nothing was changed*.
The editor stays *responsive* the whole time.
The backup's diff arrives for review, and I reject it.
git status is *clean*: the preview never touched the disk.
